text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- If prime minister-designate Mesut Yilmaz fails to win parliamentary support for a coalition, the president will appoint parliament speaker Mustafa Kalemli to form a government.
- A recently privatised tyre company has become the scene of a dispute between employers and workers over wage rises.
- Tansu Ciller, junior partner in the outgoing Islamist-led coalition, closes the door on a call by her conservative rival Mesut Yilmaz for a secularist coalition.
- An election economy is emerging with interest rates rising while the outgoing government pays out wage rises and raises the base prices of agricultural products.
- Islamist caretaker prime minister Necmettin Erbakan opens the way for thousands of his Welfare Party members to take up state posts with a decree on public appointments.
- The general manager of leading state bank Ziraat Bankasi says it is being run down by the failure of the public sector to repay its debts.
- Islamist leader Erbakan and his conservative ally Ciller seek to present a petition to the president of 280 votes against a secularist coalition, but some MPs in their parties have not signed up.
- Industry and commerce are planning their budgets in line with expectations for an early election.
- Turkish military leaders are prepared to hold more briefings on financial support for Islamist activists after caretaker prime minister Erbakan said there was no threat from religious activism.
- The sale of state bank Etibank is cancelled after the agreed buyer fails to make the necessary downpayment.
- Secularist Yilmaz's talks with party leaders on forming a secularist coalition have changed nothing as his rival Ciller continues to oppose a government led by him.
